display.purpose: The page title, with a 3px mark rule below it.

section.purpose: h2 headings, with a 2px mark rule below them (1px on a chart panel).

data.purpose: Table cells, with tabular figures. Totals use 800.

label.purpose: Table heads and filter labels. Not uppercase and not letter-spaced.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Below 600px: short day labels in the week grid, 16px side padding, and the free-agent table hides its wide columns.

breakpoints.name: drawer
breakpoints.purpose: Below 900px: the side menu becomes a drawer under a 48px top bar.

breakpoints.name: one-column
breakpoints.purpose: Below 1100px: each Home page row and the About section go to one column.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Tailored Box Score"**, in the form **Card Back**.

Each page reads like the back of a basketball card: white coated stock, royal-blue ink for the rules and the headings, and card red for alerts. The print is flat two-ink offset color, with no gradients and no shadows. In the dark theme, the stock turns to a deep navy card back with white ink. The owner approved this identity on 2026-10-28 (#117). The approved sample is `.impeccable/review/sample-index.html`.
keyCharacteristics: One token source: `src/fantasyhoops/core/tokens.py`. Pages hold no literal colors.
One family, Archivo, self-hosted next to each page in `fonts/`. Heavy condensed caps for names and headings. A sturdy grotesk with tabular figures for data.
A royal-blue side menu on a desktop. A top bar with a drawer on a phone.
Square corners. Rules, not boxes or shadows, give the page its structure.
Light and dark themes follow `prefers-color-scheme`. The Auto, Light and Dark switch in the menu sets `data-theme` on `<html>` and keeps the choice in `localStorage`.

rules.name: The One Source Rule
rules.body: A new color goes into `core/tokens.py` with a light value and a dark value. A page never writes a hex value.

rules.name: The Text Accent Rule
rules.body: As text color, `mark` shows only the page title, links, the heads of the Roster-look tables, and the selected or sorted state. Pressed chips are a solid `mark` block. The sorted column and the selected day have `mark` text and a 3px `mark` bar under the header. The teams of an add cell in the week grid are buttons, so they show as `mark` text with an underline, as a link. Other marks (the fit square, the band and the start square of the week grid, the FA?, MIN+ and UP flags) use ink.

rules.name: The Red Is Alert Rule
rules.body: `lab-red` marks only something that needs attention. It is never a decoration. A category that you trail in the matchup needs attention, so its margin is `lab-red`.

rules.name: The Green Is Lead Rule
rules.body: `lab-green` marks only a category that you lead in the matchup table. It is text only. On `zebra`, it is 5.2:1 in light and 8.1:1 in dark.

rules.name: The One Hero Rule
rules.body: Each chart has one hero mark in `mark`: the line or dot that answers the question of the chart. All other data marks use `lamp-off` at a lower weight, or `lab-red` and `lab-ink` for the dud and spike triangles.

rules.name: The Ink Only Rule
rules.body: A chart has no gridlines, no frames and no legends. Each mark in it is data, a reference line, or a direct label.

rules.name: The Thin Data Rule
rules.body: A chart that has too few games for a mark does not draw that mark. The state line says how many games the chart has and how many the mark needs.

dos: Do take each color from `core/tokens.py`, with a light value and a dark value.
Do use tabular figures for all numbers.
Do show a state with a shape, a label or a sign as well as a color.
Do keep corners square and surfaces flat.
donts: Don't write a hex value in a page generator. The draft board (`draft/board.py`) and the keeper report (`draft/report.py`) keep their own palettes. They are not on the site (owner decision of 2026-10-28).
Don't use `mark` as a text color for a mark that is not selected, sorted or a link.
Don't use side-stripe borders. A notice gets a full border.
Don't add gradients, shadows or rounded pills.
Don't draw gridlines, frames or legends in a chart.
